content_units: Anime Picks That Match the FMA:B + Haikyuu!! Vibe

You’ll likely enjoy series that combine teamwork, momentum, emotional payoffs, and strong character arcs without leaning on heavy fan service. The list below prioritizes completed or close-to-complete stories, ensemble casts, moderate accessibility for newer anime viewers, and mostly sub-80-episode runs.
10 Recommended Series
Option 1:   Mob Psycho 100     Psychic action-drama with heart, humor, and standout character growth     Beginner-friendliness: 9/10

-   Why it fits:   Like FMA:B and Haikyuu!!, it balances explosive action with sincerity, mentorship, and a lovable supporting cast. Very low fan service, emotionally clear, and complete at 37 episodes.
Option 2:   A Place Further than the Universe     A tight friendship adventure about girls aiming for Antarctica     Beginner-friendliness: 10/10

-   Why it fits:   If Haikyuu!! worked for you because of team chemistry and striving toward a huge goal, this delivers that same uplifting group energy in just 13 episodes. No horror focus, no fan-service-heavy tone, and fully complete.
Option 3:   Silver Spoon     School-life coming-of-age story from the creator of Fullmetal Alchemist     Beginner-friendliness: 9/10
-   Why it fits:   Hiromu Arakawa’s strength with ensembles, humor, and grounded growth is all over this. It’s gentler than FMA:B, but the cast dynamic and personal development feel very familiar.
Option 4:   Run with the Wind     College relay team drama with excellent camaraderie and payoff     Beginner-friendliness: 9/10

-   Why it fits:   This is one of the best follow-ups to Haikyuu!! if you want team-building, motivation, and underdog momentum. Strong ensemble, mature tone, complete in 23 episodes, and little to no distracting fan service.
Option 5:   Baccano!     Fast, stylish ensemble crime-action story with intersecting plotlines     Beginner-friendliness: 7/10

-   Why it fits:   If you liked FMA:B’s big cast and well-connected plotting, this offers a clever ensemble puzzle with energy and personality. It’s more nonlinear, so slightly less beginner-easy, but still short and complete.
Option 6:   Parasyte: The Maxim     Sci-fi thriller with moral conflict and character transformation     Beginner-friendliness: 8/10

-   Why it fits:   It shares FMA:B’s interest in humanity, ethics, and personal cost, with moderate-to-strong violence but not a horror-first identity. Complete in 24 episodes and not fan-service-driven.
Option 7:   Vivy: Fluorite Eye’s Song     Compact sci-fi action series with strong pacing and emotional core     Beginner-friendliness: 8/10
-   Why it fits:   Great if you want polished action, clear stakes, and a complete story without filler. Less ensemble-focused than others here, but very accessible and cleanly told in 13 episodes.
Option 8:   Kekkai Sensen     Urban supernatural action with chaotic but lovable team chemistry     Beginner-friendliness: 7/10

-   Why it fits:   Strong ensemble appeal, energetic battles, and a fun found-family vibe. It can be a little wild stylistically, but it avoids heavy fan service and stays well under your episode preference.
Option 9:   Dororo     Historical fantasy journey with strong emotional stakes     Beginner-friendliness: 8/10

-   Why it fits:   This works well if what you loved in FMA:B was the emotional seriousness and forward momentum. It’s darker than Haikyuu!!, but not horror-focused, complete in 24 episodes, and not fan-service-heavy.
Option 10:   86 Eighty-Six     War drama with tactical action and a strong group dynamic     Beginner-friendliness: 8/10

-   Why it fits:   It has the teamwork, sacrifice, and emotional ensemble writing that can click with both FMA:B and sports-anime fans. Moderate violence, very little fan service, and currently a strong near-complete watch at 23 episodes aired.
Best Matches to Start With
-   Most likely slam-dunk:     Mob Psycho 100
-   Closest to Haikyuu!! team-energy:     Run with the Wind
-   Closest in creator sensibility to FMA:B:     Silver Spoon
-   Best short emotional ride:     A Place Further than the Universe
-   Best if you want more action/drama:     86 Eighty-Six
Quick Start Order
- Start with   Mob Psycho 100   if you want the safest all-around recommendation.
- Pick   Run with the Wind   if you mainly want the teamwork/high-payoff sports feeling.
- Pick   Silver Spoon   if you want character writing closest in spirit to FMA:B.
- Pick   Parasyte   or   86   if you want a slightly more intense tone without horror emphasis.
Context for This List

I prioritized series that are complete or feel satisfying at their current stopping point, avoid strong fan-service-heavy presentation, and stay under or around your episode preference. A few picks are slightly more intense or stylistically unusual, but all fit your stated guardrails better than the average mainstream recommendation.
